objectives: Separate storage path, media, and array-state evidence.
Distinguish seating and population evidence from a failed DIMM.
Distinguish a connection state from a failed supply.
Separate boot selection from device detection and media state.
Use telemetry and physical evidence to isolate the cooling path.
Separate physical link evidence from address configuration.
Identify a socket-location fault without condemning known-good processors or memory.
Use cross-bay known-good comparisons to isolate a shared distribution fault.
Treat predictive failure as actionable while protecting data and proving completed recovery.
Separate read-only evidence preservation from the state-changing Repair that clears a stale alert.
Use repeated version A/B behavior and hardware elimination to diagnose a firmware regression.
Bound dangerous controller recovery to approved platform methods and verify recovery separately from the flash action.

public_context_parts.short_description: Storage operations report errors while the path remains intermittently visible.
The array reports reduced redundancy and a member needs isolation.
Firmware reports less memory than the installed configuration expects.
Workloads crash sporadically and memory remains a plausible cause.
One redundant power path is not available to the server.
One redundant supply path reports an active fault.
The server selects an unintended boot source.
POST completes, but the expected system device is not detected.
Processor temperature rises above the expected operating range.
Processor temperature remains high while the cooling path is investigated.
The server cannot reach expected network destinations.
The interface is present, but expected network destinations are unreachable.

public_context_parts.display_name: Processor Population Will Not Complete Startup
public_context_parts.short_description: The server starts with a reduced processor population but does not complete startup with the expected processors installed.

public_context_parts.display_name: Voltage Alert and Immediate Power Loss
public_context_parts.short_description: The server reports an out-of-range voltage and shuts down immediately despite supported supply substitutions.
An online array member reports predictive failure and an alternating drive-bay warning indication.

public_context_parts.display_name: Healthy Hardware Retains a Degraded Alert
public_context_parts.short_description: Current drive and enclosure checks are healthy while management continues to display an earlier degraded-backplane alert.

public_context_parts.display_name: Network Link Flaps After Firmware Change
public_context_parts.short_description: Management reports repeated link transitions after a firmware update even though substituted hardware and cabling remain stable.

public_context_parts.display_name: Management Controller Fails After Interrupted Update
public_context_parts.short_description: The embedded management controller stops responding after an interrupted firmware update while the board still exposes an approved recovery state.

findings.public_summary: The storage connector is visibly not fully latched.
The expected device disappears on the affected storage path.
Drive health data independently identifies the failed SAS member.
Array status identifies the affected member and degraded virtual disk.
smartctl corroborates the failed member health result.
Single-DIMM isolation independently identifies the unseated module path.
The DIMM seating geometry is visibly uneven.
The memory diagnostic repeatedly identifies the same failed DIMM.
The instability follows the isolated DIMM.
Management events corroborate errors from the same DIMM.
The PSU latch and chassis line do not show full seating.
The supply reports intermittent presence without an internal failure code.
A known-good supply restores the affected power path.
Supply status reports an internal failure on the affected PSU.
The approved output measurement is outside the specified range.
Firmware settings place an unintended device before the system volume.
The expected system volume is detected but is not selected first.
Management events independently identify the failed NVMe device.
The expected NVMe device is absent from storage inventory.
Firmware cannot enumerate the expected boot device.
Fan telemetry independently identifies the stalled fan.
The fault follows the fan during controlled cross-substitution.
Temperature behavior independently identifies a restricted heatsink path.
Dust visibly obstructs the heatsink airflow path.
Link returns with a known-good cable and fails again with the original cable.
The interface reports no carrier on the affected link.
The configured address and prefix do not match the authored network.
Reachability fails in the pattern expected from the incorrect static configuration.
Magnified inspection localizes visibly displaced contacts at the failing socket.
Known-good processor combinations boot away from the affected socket, contradicting a general board failure.
The processors operate in alternate supported combinations, contradicting a processor seating explanation.
The failure remains location-bound rather than following the reduced memory set.
The reduced memory comparison does not carry the startup failure away from the socket.
Known-good supplies reproduce the same failure in every supported bay, confirming the shared distribution path.
Both known-good supplies behave identically across bays, ruling out an individual supply failure.
The documented input path remains correctly connected during the reduced-configuration comparison.
Supported supplies are fully seated in each tested bay.
Controller and device health evidence confirms a predictive threshold on the identified online member.
The member remains online and responsive rather than presenting as a fully failed drive.
Preserved timestamps and healthy current telemetry show that the displayed alert describes historical state.
Fresh inventory shows the expected drives and bays healthy, contradicting a live backplane-path failure.
The failure begins with the new version set and an approved rollback removes it.
A defined soak is clean after rollback and the later upgrade reproduces the link regression.
The link path remains connected throughout the controlled comparison.
Known-good cabling does not carry the failure away from the affected firmware state.
Hardware substitutions do not carry the failure, ruling out an individual interface fault.
Approved recovery-state checks confirm controller firmware corruption without prescribing a board-specific raw procedure.
Platform and image compatibility checks rule out an ordinary incompatible-version set.

The array returns to a healthy redundant state.
Expected memory capacity and channel inventory are restored.
A complete memory test passes after reseating.
A complete memory test passes without the original errors.
The redundant power path remains stable after reseating.
The replacement supply remains stable under normal operation.
The server boots from the intended system volume.
The replacement NVMe device is detected.
The server completes a normal boot from the replacement device.
Fan telemetry and temperature remain normal under controlled load.
Processor temperature remains within range under controlled load.
The repaired interface maintains physical carrier.
Expected network destinations are reachable.
The corrected interface reaches the expected destinations.
Repeated cold starts complete with every expected processor and memory channel present and no new socket-path event.
Cold starts, bay telemetry, and a safe redundancy transition complete without a new voltage or power-good event.
The documented replacement member is present, rebuild completes, the array is healthy, and no predictive warning returns.
After evidence-preserving state refresh, current hardware stays healthy and the target alert does not recur during the defined window.
The approved version set persists after restart and the defined link/counter soak completes without the regression.
The approved recovery completes and the controller reaches the reported reset and normal-start acceptance boundary.
